title: Offer to help young musicians; age 65 with the World's Greatest Jazz Band
summary: Leeman gives his phone number, says he wants to help anyone interested, and says he still plays strongly for an hour and a half at age 65.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Well, what I'm trying to say and what I'm trying to find out -- for a matter of record, that these young people love you, and they would like to come to you.
I'd welcome them with open arms.

Thank you. On this tape, as a matter of record, knowing you to be the great musician you are, and the great musician that you -- the great things that you perform, that you would be willing to help them in any kind of way.
On my publicity releases, it says Cliff Leeman - 21-04 154th Street, White Stone, New York 11357. Telephone number 358-2504 -- for 28 years. I've got time.

And I'm interested -- if I can help anybody in any way, I've got a few tricks and a few things to talk about. Maybe I can help somebody, maybe they would like, out of curiosity, to talk to me. But it'd be nice if they could see me work, still. I'm 65 years old -- I'd like to have them see me work, because there are a lot of cats 65 years old who are limping around, and I don't show it. I don't show it, but I can scare somebody for an hour and a half or two hours, and I'm doing it all the time in the World's Greatest Jazz Band. I don't want to play until three or four o'clock in the morning -- because I give my whole heart and soul for an hour and a half or two hours, and I think that's all that's asking me. You see kids today with the heavy rock and everything; they kill themselves for two hours, and they're done. Well, we used to play for hours, until four o'clock in the morning. But I'd love to have anybody contact me. I gave
you the whole thing -- for 28 years I've been in the phone book with that same number -- 358-2504 -- exchanged ...
